source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What is the normal serum sodium range?
questions.rationale: Sodium 135–145; potassium 3.5–5.5 mEq/L.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Normal Electrolytes (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: Sodium — 135-145 mEq/L

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Movement of water from low to high solute concentration is:
questions.rationale: Osmosis moves solvent; diffusion moves solute from high to low.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluid Movement (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: OSMOSIS — movement of SOLVENT; low to high concentration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why are infants and older adults at higher risk of fluid imbalance?
questions.rationale: Infants are about 80% water; elderly have less muscle and diminished thirst.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluid Balance Factors (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: ELDERLY — less muscle; thirst center diminished

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A dehydrated client's hematocrit is likely to be:
questions.rationale: Too little fluid causes hemoconcentration and high hematocrit.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Lab Tests (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: too little fluid in the blood will cause hemoconcentration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on furosemide has muscle weakness and a U wave on ECG. The likely imbalance is:
questions.rationale: Diuretics cause K loss: weakness, flat T, prominent U wave.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypokalemia (PDF p. 395)
questions.quote: prominent U wave, flat T wave

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Tall, peaked T waves in a client with renal failure suggest:
questions.rationale: Hyperkalemia causes peaked T waves, widened QRS, and V-fib risk.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperkalemia (PDF p. 396)
questions.quote: peaked, narrow T waves

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which condition shifts potassium out of cells, causing hyperkalemia?
questions.rationale: In acidosis, H+ moves into cells and K+ moves out.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hyperkalemia (PDF p. 396)
questions.quote: acidosis also can cause hyperkalemia

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with SIADH becomes confused and has a seizure. The likely cause is:
questions.rationale: Dilutional hyponatremia causes headache, confusion, seizures, coma.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hyponatremia (PDF p. 397)
questions.quote: Patients with conditions that result in excessive retention of fluid, such as the syndrome of inappropriate antidiuretic hormone

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Thirst, dry mucous membranes, and irritability with serum Na 152 mEq/L indicate:
questions.rationale: Hypernatremia: thirst, dehydration signs, neurologic irritability.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypernatremia (PDF p. 397)
questions.quote: Complaints of thirst

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Prolonged gastric suctioning can cause hypochloremia and:
questions.rationale: Loss of HCl from suction or vomiting causes metabolic alkalosis.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypochloremia (PDF p. 397)
questions.quote: gastric suctioning (resulting in loss of acid and metabolic alkalosis)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which ECG change is associated with hypocalcemia?
questions.rationale: Hypocalcemia prolongs QT; hypercalcemia shortens it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypocalcemia (PDF p. 398)
questions.quote: ECG: Prolonged QT interval

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client with bone metastases has nausea, weakness, and somnolence. The nurse suspects:
questions.rationale: Bone cancer releases calcium; hypercalcemia causes anorexia, weakness, somnolence.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypercalcemia (PDF p. 398)
questions.quote: from cancer in the bone releasing calcium into the bloodstream

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Chronic alcohol use and loop diuretics commonly cause:
questions.rationale: Alcohol and diuretics increase urinary magnesium loss.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypomagnesemia (PDF p. 398)
questions.quote: alcohol abuse

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Overuse of magnesium-containing antacids in renal failure may cause:
questions.rationale: Excess intake with decreased excretion raises magnesium: weakness, hypotension.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Hypermagnesemia (PDF p. 399)
questions.quote: specifically found in antacids

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Phosphate and calcium have which relationship?
questions.rationale: High phosphate means low calcium, and vice versa.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Phosphate (PDF p. 399)
questions.quote: High Phosphate=Low Calcium; Low Phosphate=High Calcium

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Normal arterial pH is:
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Arterial Blood Gases (PDF p. 399)
questions.quote: NORMAL BLOOD PH: 7.35-7.45

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which finding suggests fluid volume deficit?
questions.rationale: FVD: flat neck veins, tachycardia, orthostatic hypotension, concentrated urine.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluid Volume Deficit (PDF p. 400)
questions.quote: Flattened neck veins

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which IV fluid is used to expand plasma volume in a hypotensive dehydrated client?
questions.rationale: Isotonic solutions (NS, LR) expand plasma volume.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FVD Management (PDF p. 400)
questions.quote: Frequently used to treat the hypotensive patient with FVD

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: In fluid volume deficit, BUN is typically:
questions.rationale: BUN rises out of proportion to creatinine in hypovolemia.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FVD Diagnostics (PDF p. 400)
questions.quote: BUN elevated out of proportion to the serum creatinine

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A weight gain of 1 kg overnight equals about how much retained fluid?
questions.rationale: 1 kg (2.2 lb) gain equals about 1 L of fluid.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FVE Management (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Weight gain of 2.2 lb (1 kg) is equivalent to a gain of approximately 1 L of fluid.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Distended neck veins, crackles, and bounding pulse indicate:
questions.rationale: Hypervolemia: edema, JVD, crackles, increased BP and CVP.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Fluid Volume Excess (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Distended neck veins

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which diuretic may cause hyperkalemia?
questions.rationale: Potassium-sparing diuretics acting in the distal tubule can raise K.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FVE Management (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Hyperkalemia can occur with diuretics that work in the last distal tubule (eg, spironolactone)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client on a sodium-restricted diet should be taught to:
questions.rationale: Read labels and avoid OTC drugs that may contain sodium.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, FVE Management (PDF p. 401)
questions.quote: Patients are instructed to read food labels carefully
